_what: Rate card for the models the benchmark legs actually use. Read off the LiteLLM admin UI's per-model detail pages on 2026-09-17. Consumed by reference/gen-cost-analysis.py; no generator may hardcode a price.
_amended: 2026-09-29: the four models above had all been WITHDRAWN from the gateway's catalogue -- `GET /v1/models` no longer lists any of them -- so they price past runs only and nothing new can be measured with them. The four `_added_2026_09_29` rows below replace them role for role and were read from the gateway's own unauthenticated `GET /public/litellm_model_cost_map`, not from the admin UI. Same basis either way: both report the upstream list rate (gpt-5-mini reads 0.25/2.00 in both), so rows from the two sources are comparable. A run priced with the new rows is NOT comparable with the v1.28 matrix -- every model differs.
_keys: Keyed by the EXACT `model` string in report.ndjson, which carries litellm's `openai/` routing prefix. That prefix is not part of the model's name -- the gateway strips it before resolving the alias in `public_name`.
_caveats: Input and output only. The UI's model pages expose no cached-input tier, so a cache-read discount -- if the gateway applies one -- is not modelled and every figure computed from this file is an upper bound on input cost.
Reasoning tokens are billed as output. gpt-5-mini is a reasoning model, and our llm_output_tokens already includes its exposed reasoning tokens, so no separate term is needed.
These are the gateway operator's posted rates, not an invoice. They are what a run WOULD cost at list price.

openai/Azure/gpt-4.1._also: The IBAC judge model (rossoctl-platform-config ibac.judgeModel). Its calls are NOT in report.ndjson -- see gen-cost-analysis.py's judge section.

openai/aws/claude-sonnet-5._role_2026_09_30: The INTRANET (vpc-int) tau2 role, counterpart to aws/claude-sonnet-4-6 on vpc: no Sonnet ID is served by both gateways, and this is the only Sonnet vpc-int carries that is priced here. It is also registry.py's own model_override for tau2, so INTRANET_LLM_MODEL_TAU2 restates what that pod resolves anyway -- set explicitly because the same variable is the only lever that displaces the override on vpc, where it is NOT served. Consequence: tau2 legs #9/#10 run a different model per platform at ~half the price of the vpc side (1.52/7.60 vs 3.00/15.00), so tau2 DOLLAR figures do not compare across clusters even when the token counts do.

openai/gemini-2.5-pro._assumed: Priced from the rate card's `gcp/gemini-2.5-pro` entry (vertex_ai/gemini-2.5-pro, $1.25/$10.00). Our legs send the BARE alias `gemini-2.5-pro`, which is a separate registration on the gateway and the only Gemini 2.5 Pro our key can see; `/model/info` is admin-only (403), so its backend was not read directly. If the bare alias is ever repointed, this row is the one that goes stale.

openai/azure/gpt-5.6-luna._added_2026_09_29: Replaces Azure/gpt-5-mini as the INSTANCE DEFAULT, so it prices gsm8k legs #1-#3 and #5-#8. Cheaper than the model it replaces on both directions (0.25/2.00), so a gsm8k leg's cost is not directly comparable with the v1.28 figure even at identical token counts.
openai/azure/gpt-5.6-luna._also: Also the IBAC judge model from 2026-09-29 (rossoctl-platform-config ibac.judgeModel), taking over from Azure/gpt-4.1. Judge calls are NOT in report.ndjson -- see gen-cost-analysis.py's judge section. The judge is now an order of magnitude cheaper per call than it was, which moves the plugin-overhead cost figures on its own, independently of any change in call COUNT.
openai/azure/gpt-5.6-luna._backend_not_read: `/model/info` is admin-only (403) for an ['llm_api_routes'] key, so which Azure deployment sits behind this alias was not read. `litellm_model` is therefore omitted rather than guessed.
openai/azure/gpt-5.6-luna._role_2026_09_30: Not used for tau2: registry.py records that tau2 needs a Sonnet-class model (the old default gpt-5-mini scored ~0.1 on the same 10 tasks; the slower reasoning model gpt-5 gave 6/10 'timed out'), and the vpc/vpc-int Sonnets carry that role instead. NOTE this is registry.py's recorded measurement, not something re-measured in 2026-09-30's tau2 runs -- those hit an unrelated MODEL-INDEPENDENT failure (see aws/claude-sonnet-4-6's _tau2_task0_2026_09_30), so they say nothing either way about luna's tau2 capability.

openai/azure/gpt-5.6-terra._added_2026_09_29: Replaces Azure/gpt-4.1 in the gsm8k model-swap leg (#4). Input matches what it replaces exactly (2.00); output is 12.00 against 8.00. Against the new default it is 10x input and 10x output, so it still plays the 'dearer rung' role the leg exists to measure -- but the RATIO changed (gpt-4.1 was 8x/4x over gpt-5-mini), which is the figure to re-derive rather than carry over.
openai/azure/gpt-5.6-terra._role_2026_09_30: Also the INTRANET (vpc-int) appworld role, because vpc-int serves no gemini. Priced identically to gcp/gemini-3.1-pro-preview (2.00/12.00), so appworld COST comparisons across platforms still hold even though the token counts belong to different models. Note this model now plays two roles on the intranet profile -- the gsm8k swap leg #4 and appworld #11/#12.

openai/aws/claude-sonnet-4-6._added_2026_09_29: Replaces aws/claude-sonnet-5 on the tau2 legs (#9, #10) -- the only Sonnet the catalogue now carries, and a LOWER version number than the withdrawn one. Roughly 2x the price it replaces (1.52/7.60), so tau2 cost figures move up even where token counts hold.
openai/aws/claude-sonnet-4-6._tau2_task0_2026_09_30: tau2 TASK 0 IS BROKEN UPSTREAM, on the MCP side and independently of the model -- so it is not a pricing property of this model, only the row it was measured on. ykt5 2026-09-30, 4 attempts / 2 models: task 0 errors EVERY time with 'Failed to run mcp call {error: Failed to execute action: timed out}' after llm_count 1 and tool_total_s 600.1 -- twice on azure/gpt-5.6-luna, twice on this model. Other tasks pass alongside it (1/2/3 at 3/6/20 llm calls). Two alternatives were ruled out rather than argued: (1) NOT a bad task -- v1.28 leg #9 passed task 0 on 2026-09-15 with 92670 in / 12 calls, and the task set is pinned to upstream tag v0.1.3; (2) NOT the ETE gateway stall biting the MCP pod's first user-simulator call -- a 4-task run at parallelism 4 started all four sessions at the same instant (20:59:05.199) and task 0 alone still failed, so nothing about being first explains it. The 600 s cap is not ours either: we send benchmark.action_timeout=1000 (echoed by the MCP pod) and the Service task timeout was 1200 on these runs. Image was exgentic-mcp-tau2@sha256:1846bdc82802d6327684c3ed45e653d7692437030b75909d408a992caff6ad41 (:latest, so it moved since v1.28); agent was exgentic-a2a-tool_calling@sha256:6f70f41fa9e9871bf5cf545548e19de812e454768e0f32dbdec7506b65008914. CONSEQUENCE FOR PRICING: task selection is deterministic from 0, so every tau2 leg now carries one guaranteed errored task -- use a (total - 1) denominator for tau2 pass rates until this clears, and count its ~4.2k tokens as real spend that bought no verdict.

openai/gcp/gemini-3.1-pro-preview._added_2026_09_29: Replaces gemini-2.5-pro on the appworld legs (#11, #12); same family, two minor versions on. Unlike the row it replaces this is the gateway's PREFIXED registration, not a bare alias, so it is the name the cost map actually carries and needs no assumed-pricing note. A `-preview` alias is repointed by its vendor without warning -- re-read this row before pricing a new appworld run.
